question: What is a polyvalent nurse mainly trained to do?
explanation: You've got this! A polyvalent nurse is multi-skilled, meaning they can comfortably work across different healthcare specialties instead of being restricted to just one. It's a great asset on the ward! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of having polyvalent nurses in a hospital?

options.A: Elimination of the need for doctor consultations
options.B: Flexibility to cover different patient care units
options.C: Reduction in the total number of hospital beds
options.D: Lowering the required training period for students

explanation: Because their training is broad, hospitals can easily deploy them wherever staff are needed most to keep patient care running smoothly. Makes scheduling much easier! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a key skill required of a polyvalent nurse?

options.D: Mastery of a single surgical subspecialty

explanation: Spot on! Clinical versatility is just another way of saying they can adapt their skills to whatever ward or patient needs they encounter. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is continuous learning so important for a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Medical equipment never changes after initial installation
options.B: Hospital management requires daily written examinations
options.C: Specialized nurses do not need to update their skills
options.D: They must maintain competence across many different clinical areas

explanation: Since they move between various specialties, staying up to date on multiple fields of medicine helps them provide safe, top-notch care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: Adaptability in polyvalent nursing mostly helps the nurse deal with...

options.B: Eliminating all challenges in rural clinics
options.C: Fixed schedules in a single laboratory room
options.D: Predictable patient loads every single day

explanation: Nursing is dynamic! Adaptability means you can roll with the punches when moving between different clinical settings and resource levels. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: A polyvalent nurse moves from a city hospital to a rural clinic. What action shows good adaptability?

options.A: Treating patients using only strict urban protocols
options.B: Waiting for senior doctors to manage basic dressings
options.C: Modifying care plans to match available local resources
options.D: Refusing to work until city-standard equipment arrives

explanation: Brilliant! Adapting means using what's available locally to deliver safe, effective care without letting a lack of fancy equipment stop you. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: Good communication for a polyvalent nurse helps most with...

options.B: Collaborating effectively with various healthcare teams
options.C: Reducing the number of nursing shifts per week
options.D: Replacing the need for patient medical records

explanation: Communication is key in healthcare. Working across different specialties means chatting clearly with diverse professionals to keep patient care coordinated. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is a quick and concise patient handover so critical for a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift reports
options.B: It shortens the working hours of the incoming shift
options.C: It stops doctors from reviewing patient charts
options.D: It prevents clinical errors during department transitions

explanation: Good handovers ensure vital patient details don't slip through the cracks when patients or nurses move between different units. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary way critical thinking helps a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Rely entirely on memorized textbook answers
options.B: Manage sudden changes in patient conditions
options.C: Delegate all thinking tasks to junior staff
options.D: Avoid making clinical decisions on the ward

explanation: You got it! Critical thinking lets you assess fast-moving, complex situations on the ward and take the right action quickly. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: If a polyvalent nurse faces an unfamiliar medical device in a new ward, what should they do?

options.A: Ignore the device and use traditional manual methods
options.B: Use core safety principles and seek proper guidance
options.C: Refuse the duty assignment until next week
options.D: Operate it immediately without checking instructions

explanation: Safety first! Recognizing when you need guidance and taking proactive steps to learn safely is a mark of a great professional. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical duty of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Ignoring patient confidentiality in busy wards
options.C: Recognizing personal limits in clinical competence
options.D: Advocating for the rights of sick individuals

explanation: Spot on! Patient confidentiality is sacred. Ignoring it is a serious breach of professional ethics, no matter how busy the ward gets. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why must a polyvalent nurse be mindful of their scope of practice?

options.A: To avoid interacting with medical doctors
options.C: To ensure they only work day shifts
options.D: To prevent harm from performing unfamiliar procedures

explanation: Knowing your limits keeps patients safe from procedures you aren't yet trained to do. Always stay within your safe zone! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)

question: What major challenge in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help address?

options.A: The complete absence of patient illness
options.B: Staffing shortages in various health facilities
options.C: Excessive medical equipment in rural clinics
options.D: An overabundance of specialized intensive care units

explanation: Exactly! By being flexible and multi-skilled, polyvalent nurses help bridge the gap when health facilities are short-staffed. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h7)

question: How do polyvalent nurses improve healthcare delivery in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: By restricting patient admissions to surgical cases only
options.B: By replacing all local community health workers permanently
options.C: By working exclusively in private urban hospitals
options.D: By managing diverse health needs with a flexible skill set

explanation: Well done! Their broad training means they can handle a wide variety of medical needs in communities where specialists might not be around. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h7)
